correctness.rationale: The proof establishes scalar-coupling lift, elementary four-class sign-group matching for all 3x3 real symmetric matrices, binomial complete-graph law, exact Walsh covariance under every mask and a strict crossed-order certificate for all dimensions at least four. The two independent exact arithmetic implementations agree through n=12, and checker passes 832 assertions; finite checks are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Named primary sources establish independent-probe bounds, low-rank Hutch++, and coloring-based probing but do not state the sharp four-vertex obstruction or all-complete-graph strict coupling gap. The scalar antitone rearrangement inequality is fully acknowledged as classical; the precise low-dimensional rigidity and binomial family classification are the claimed contribution. Relevant related weighted-five-cycle claim was checked for implication and does not cover arbitrary 3x3 or complete graphs. An earlier direct classification remains possible.
residual_risks: Classical rearrangement and standard binomial computations could have been combined explicitly in an earlier specialist treatment not located by these queries.
One later Hutch++ variant was examined at abstract level only; there is no evidence it is a direct coverage match.
The result describes a class-constrained variance optimum and not algorithmic speedups or unrestricted query complexity.

value.rationale: The first dimension at which no fixed coordinate sign flip is globally variance-optimal is a natural sharp boundary for a common low-cost antithetic design. The unweighted four-vertex complete graph example is the smallest symmetric-matrix witness, and the infinite complete-graph family has exact variance and asymptotic formulae. It quantifies the avoidable gap between mask design and joint-law design without claiming better runtime or unrestricted estimator optimality.
